summary: High 5xx surge caused by ephemeral-worker thrash driving proxy accept-queue collapse
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 08:12 UTC we observed a rapid spike in 5xx responses from the hosted API for a subset of dedicated tenants. The spike manifested as short, high-amplitude waves of 502/503 and backend connection resets.
impact: Customer-facing: multiple ScribeAI customers experienced elevated error rates (up to 18% 5xx across their routes) for ~45 minutes. Throughput degraded and some long-lived streaming sessions were terminated. Internal alerting triggered SLO-error pages for us-east.
observed_behavior:
- API Gateway returning 502/503 on new requests to hot routes.
- Serving runtime logs show repeated 'worker process exited' and 'prefetch cancel' messages.
- Ephemeral worker pool churn: high create/destroy rate for ephemeral workers feeding prefetch + warmup paths.
- Proxy accept-queue length exceeded configured threshold followed by connection resets (RST) to upstreams.
expected_behavior: Stable 2xx responses with bounded rate of ephemeral-worker recycling and healthy proxy accept-queue lengths under the sustained tenant traffic profile.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Target the dedicated tenant's hot route with a steady ramp to 350 rps and a mix of short streaming and sync generation requests.
2) Observe accept-queue metrics and ephemeral-worker churn.
3) Increase concurrency on clients to reproduce unstable backpressure behavior.
(Replication performed in staging with synthetic load.)

investigation_notes:
Timeline: 08:12 alerts began; SRE auto-scaling did not immediately trigger because ephemeral pool hit a recycle threshold instead of utilization threshold. Investigation showed a feedback loop: slow prefetch warms caused worker recycle -> new workers create short-lived connections -> proxy accept queue grows -> connection churning increases latency and triggers runtime watchdog OOMs.
Hypotheses tested: 1) Kernel-level socket limit (no). 2) NVMe iowait hotspot (no). 3) Backpressure misconfiguration between apigw and ephemeral worker pool (yes).
Metrics inspected: accept_queue_length, ephemeral_worker_create_rate, prefetch_latency, runtime_heap_usage. Correlation: sharp rise in ephemeral create/destroy rate preceded 5xx onset by ~30s.
Relevant crossrefs: observability board link, Slack #support-thread (https://slack.redwood/threads/C12345), and runtime PR 2124 which introduced a recent prefetch worker recycle heuristic.
workaround: Applied immediate mitigations at 08:22: - Enabled conservative backoff on apigw: limit concurrent handoffs to hot upstreams. - Temporarily raised accept_queue size for prod us-east proxies. - Disabled aggressive ephemeral-worker recycle heuristic (feature-flag off). These actions reduced 5xx rate to baseline within 6 minutes.
resolution:
Mitigated: temporary config changes and feature-flag rollback prevented further waves. Root cause: an aggressive ephemeral-worker recycle heuristic (recent hotpatch) combined with a mismatch in apigw->ephemeral backpressure knobs. The recycle pattern created connection churn that collapsed the proxy accept queue and triggered cascading runtime restarts.
Fix plan: - Rework recycle heuristic to consider accept-queue and prefetch latency signals (ENG-3245). - Add rate-limited backpressure at apigw to prevent accept-queue exhaustion (APIGW-198). - Add SLO-aware autoscaler rule to act on worker churn (AUTO-77).
Rollout notes: all changes to be staged in canary in us-east on 2026-03-14, with 2h blast radius, rollback via feature-flag.
Follow-up: runbook update, synthetic test to replicate churn and validate guard rails, postmortem doc scheduled.
next_steps:
1) ENG to review and merge PR to change recycle logic (owner: Daniel Kim, ETA: 2026-03-16).
2) SRE to add alert for ephemeral_create_rate > X and accept_queue_len > Y (owner: Maria Gonzalez, ETA: 2026-03-13).
3) Product to coordinate tenant communication and credits if needed (owner: Sofia Martinez).
